commonMistakes: A partly correct response can still miss a required form, unit, relationship or mark point.
detailedExplanation: Plants use glucose in several ways: - respiration to transfer energy; - converted to starch for storage; - converted to cellulose for cell walls; - combined with nitrate ions to make amino acids, which are used to make proteins; - converted to lipids/oils for storage, especially in seeds.
Starch is useful for storage because it is insoluble and therefore does not strongly affect water movement by osmosis.
